sentences.text:
By way of preferring the present applications under Section 528 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, the applicants-accused seek to invoke the inherent powers of this Court,
praying to quash and set-aside the First Information Report No. 11196001210013 of 2021 registered with the Mahila Police Station, Vadodara City, for the offences punishable under Sections 498A,
323, 354A, 504, 506, 114 of the Indian Penal Code and under Sections 3, 7 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, as well as all other consequential proceedings arising pursuant thereto.
3.
Today, when the matter is called out, the complainant, who is personally present before this Court, has submitted her affidavit in each of the applications.
The same is ordered to be taken on record.

In the said affidavit, the complainant has categorically stated that with the intervention of the friends, family members and community people, the dispute between the parties has been amicably resolved and there is no ill-will or any grievance amongst them.

4. Considering the issue involved in the present applications as well as considering the fact that the dispute has been amicably resolved between the parties, with the consent of the learned advocates appearing for the respective parties, the present applications are taken up for final disposal.
5. RULE returnable forthwith.
Learned APP Mr. Manan NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/14849/2021 ORDER DATED: 24/02/2026 undefined

Maheta waives service of notice of rule for and on behalf of the respondent no.1 - State and learned advocate Mr. Nasir Saiyed waives service of notice of rule for and on behalf of the respondent no.2 - complainant in Criminal Misc.
Application Nos.14849 of 2021 and 4199 of 2021 and learned advocate Mr. Nisara Jain waives service of notice of rule for and on behalf of the respondent no.2 - complainant in Criminal Misc.
Application No.2503 of 2021.

6. Learned advocate for the applicants-accused has submitted that since the dispute has been amicably resolved between the parties, the applications may be allowed and the impugned FIR may be quashed and set-aside.
7. The complainant, who is personally present in the Court, has categorically stated before this Court that she has no objection if the applications are allowed and the FIR is quashed and set-aside.

Thus,
it appears from the aforesaid that sending the applicants-accused to face the trial would be nothing but a futile exercise and would amount to abuse of process of law.

8. The relevant paragraphs of the affidavit filed by the complainant - Pathan Minajbanu Akibkhan,
read thus :

"3. The Criminal Misc. Application No. 1551 of 2021 under Domestic Violence act,
wherein in the Lok- Adalat the matter is being settled between the parties- the applicant and the complainant have decided to separate ways and does not want to continue the proceedings and wishes to withdraw the present NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/14849/2021 ORDER DATED: 24/02/2026 undefined petition.
The copy of the order dated 13.12.2025 in Criminal Misc. Application No. 1551 of 2021 is annexed hereto and marked as Annexure- "R-1".

sentences.text: It is very respectfully submitted that the dispute between us is private in nature.
The parties herein have mutually decided to part the ways and live separately without having any grudges against each other.
Thus, the complainant wishes to withdraw the complaint against the applicant.
The complainant have already withdrawn the application filed for maintenance under Section 125 of Criminal Procedure Code.
Further, the application under Domestic Violence Act, filed by the complainant has also been withdrawn by the complainant.
Now no grievances what so ever in any nature exist between us.
The parties have entered into mutual agreement dated 28-11-2025 before the notary.

The copy of the divorce deed notarized dated 28-11-2025 is annexed hereto and marked as Annexure- "R-2"
5.
In light of the above facts and circumstances the matter is settled between the parties.

So, I have no objection if the present application being filed by the applicant is disposed off in view of the settlement between the parties and further all subsequent proceedings pursuant thereto be quashed and set aside in the interest of justice."
9.

Having heard learned advocates appearing for the respective parties as well as considering the facts and circumstances arising out of the present applications and taking into consideration the decisions rendered in the cases of Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab & Another, reported in (2012) 10 SCC 303, Madan Mohan Abbot vs. State of Punjab, reported in (2008) 4 SCC 582, Nikhil Merchant vs. Central Bureau of Investigation & Another, reported in (2009) 1 GLH 31, Manoj Sharma vs. State & Others, reported in (2009) 1 GLH 190, and Narinder Singh & Others vs. State of Punjab &
Another, reported in (2014) 2 Crime 67 (SC) as well as State of Haryana vs. Bhajanlal, reported in AIR 1992 SC 604, it

sentences.text: NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/14849/2021 ORDER DATED: 24/02/2026 undefined appears that further continuation of the criminal proceedings in relation to the impugned FIR against the applicants-accused would be nothing but unnecessary harassment to the applicants- accused.
It further appears that the trial would be a futile exercise and continuing further with the proceedings pursuant to the impugned FIR would amount to abuse of process of law.

Hence, to secure the ends of justice, the impugned FIR and all other consequential proceedings arising pursuant thereto are required to be quashed and set-aside in exercise of the powers conferred under Section 528 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.
10.
In the result, the applications are allowed.

The First Information Report No. 11196001210013 of 2021 registered with the Mahila Police Station, Vadodara City, for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 323, 354A, 504, 506, 114 of the Indian Penal Code and under Sections 3, 7 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, as well as all other consequential proceedings arising pursuant thereto are hereby ordered to be quashed and set-aside, qua the present applicants only.
11. Rule made absolute.
Direct service is permitted.
